items.title: LeBron James, the 76ers and the legacy in the balance
items.summary: So, it's the Philadelphia 76ers for LeBron James. Weird choice, right?Of all the teams, of all the places, Philadelphia? It felt like it was going to be someplace more significant, somewhere more meaningful, but it's the Sixers.I guess they give him the best chance to win a championship, because that starting lineup — James, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid — it's a bear. It's an awfully big bet on the health of Embiid, who is rarely healthy these days, but it's a bet on a championship, and that is what it's all about for LeBron at this point.After all, he's always been in pursuit of Michael Jordan's six rings."My motivation," James once told a Nike skills academy camper, according to a 2016 Sports Illustrated profile, "is this ghost I'm chasing. items.summary: This first part is where I tell you that, now that LeBron James made his decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers, it’s time for him to deliver.This second bit is where I acknowledge that we hold him to an unreasonable standard.Cruising social media in the moments after James surprised the NBA world Friday, July 24 and announced he would be joining his fourth different team, the prevailing sentiment was that a failure to deliver a championship in Philadelphia would derail James’ legacy. items.title: LeBron James and his fit with the 76ers
items.summary: The Decision 4.0 wasn't a grandiose television spectacle that captivated millions of viewers. Nor was it an emotional return home or an emboldened attempt to etch an imprint into a historic franchise's tapestry. LeBron James' resolution, choosing the Philadelphia 76ers as his fourth and final destination entering his 24th season, was a move not rooted in flash or pizazz but one centered in logic. In contention. "I still want to sacrifice," the 41-year-old said on his X account on what had been an eerily quiet Friday morning. "I still want to work. I still want to grind.
